section: Parliament - composition of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, qualifications, terms, special powers of Rajya Sabha
subsections: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS
Sessions - summoning, number in a year, maximum gap
Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122

accepted.s: Under Article 83(2) of the Constitution, the normal term of the Lok Sabha is calculated from which event?
o: The date of the President's summons
The date on which the Speaker is elected
The date of its election notification
The date of its first meeting
accepted.x: The normal five-year term of the Lok Sabha is reckoned from the date of its first meeting.
accepted.tq: Test the precise constitutional starting point rather than the commonly confused election date.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Lok Sabha may be dissolved before completion of its normal term by the President on the advice of the
accepted.x: The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha earlier on the advice of the Prime Minister. Such a dissolution cannot be challenged in court.
accepted.tq: Use the 'who would do this job?' method for executive powers.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the extension of the term of the Lok Sabha during a National Emergency, consider the following statements:
1. Parliament may extend the term by law for one year at a time.
2. The extension may continue indefinitely after the Emergency ends.
3. No extension can continue beyond six months after the Emergency has ceased.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The term may be extended by law for one year at a time during the Emergency, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ends. Statement 2 is therefore false.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the limiting phrase in the constitutional rule.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Lok Sabha was extended during the National Emergency of 1975–1977?
accepted.x: The Fifth Lok Sabha, constituted for the period 1971–1977, was extended during the 1975–1977 Emergency.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered Lok Sabhas and their distinct events.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following Lok Sabhas was dissolved before completion of its full term?
accepted.x: The Thirteenth Lok Sabha was dissolved in 2004 before completing its full term. The Fifth Lok Sabha was extended during the Emergency.
accepted.tq: Find the one item belonging to the stated group by distinguishing dissolution from extension.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs of Lok Sabhas and years of premature dissolution is correctly matched?
1. Fourth Lok Sabha — 1970
2. Sixth Lok Sabha — 1979
3. Eleventh Lok Sabha — 1997
4. Twelfth Lok Sabha — 1999
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Fourth, Sixth, Eleventh and Twelfth Lok Sabhas were dissolved prematurely in 1970, 1979, 1997 and 1999 respectively.
accepted.tq: Verify each date independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rajya Sabha:
1. It is a permanent and continuing House.
2. It is not subject to dissolution.
3. The whole House is elected together after every six years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Rajya Sabha is permanent and is never dissolved. Its members retire by rotation; the whole House is not elected together.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed comparison between the two Houses.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term of a member of the Rajya Sabha is six years. This term is fixed by the
o: Rules of Procedure of the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The six-year term of a Rajya Sabha member is fixed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and not directly by the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction to avoid an authority trap.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the first Rajya Sabha constituted in 1952, the members who were to retire first were selected by
o: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: To initiate the one-third retirement cycle, the terms of the initial members were curtailed and the members retiring first were decided by lottery.
accepted.tq: Use a precise institutional detail rather than a general feature of rotation.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many Lok Sabhas had been constituted up to the reference year 2026?
accepted.x: Eighteen Lok Sabhas had been constituted up to 2026.
accepted.tq: Handle a current numerical fact by selecting the exact count, not an approximate range.
accepted.sec: Term of each House - early dissolution, emergency extension, permanence of RS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 85(1) of the Constitution, each House of Parliament is summoned by the
accepted.x: Article 85(1) vests the power to summon each House in the President. The two Houses need not be summoned together.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'wrong authority' trap to distinguish constitutional offices.
accepted.sec: Sessions - summoning, number in a year, maximum gap  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the summoning of Parliament:
1. The President may summon the two Houses separately.
2. The Constitution requires both Houses to be summoned together on every occasion.
3. Each House must meet within six months of its previous sitting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The President need not summon both Houses together, and the maximum interval between sessions is six months. Statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the constitutional rule on separate summoning.
accepted.sec: Sessions - summoning, number in a year, maximum gap  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The maximum permissible gap between two sessions of Parliament is measured from the
o: First sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next
Last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next
Date of adjournment sine die to the date of dissolution
Date of prorogation of one session to the date of summoning of the next
accepted.x: The six-month interval is counted from the last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next session.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar session dates by focusing on the exact endpoints.
accepted.sec: Sessions - summoning, number in a year, maximum gap  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the normal pattern of parliamentary sessions in India?
o: Winter, Spring and Special sessions only
accepted.x: There is no fixed constitutional calendar, but Parliament normally has Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions.
accepted.tq: Choose the established institutional terminology rather than an invented seasonal sequence.
accepted.sec: Sessions - summoning, number in a year, maximum gap  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the calendar of parliamentary sessions is correct?
o: The Constitution fixes exactly three sessions every year.
The Speaker alone determines the number of sessions in a year.
The President must summon Parliament only in January, June and November.
There is no fixed constitutional calendar, although three sessions are normally held.
accepted.x: The Constitution does not prescribe a fixed calendar or exact number of sessions, though Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions are normally held.
accepted.tq: Watch for extreme words such as 'exactly' and 'only' in institutional statements.
accepted.sec: Sessions - summoning, number in a year, maximum gap  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who orders an adjournment sine die of a House of Parliament?
o: The Speaker or Chairman of the concerned House
The Prime Minister after consulting the Cabinet
The President in respect of both Houses
accepted.x: An adjournment sine die is ordered by the Speaker in the Lok Sabha or the Chairman in the Rajya Sabha, without fixing a date for the next sitting.
accepted.tq: Use the office-and-function matching method for parliamentary terminology.
accepted.sec: Sessions - summoning, number in a year, maximum gap  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Article 105 of the Constitution primarily deals with
o: The qualifications of Members of Parliament
The privileges and powers of Parliament and its members
The composition of the Election Commission
accepted.x: Article 105 concerns parliamentary privileges, including freedom of speech in Parliament and related immunities.
accepted.tq: Test the exact Article–subject association.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With regard to freedom of speech in Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. Article 105 protects freedom of speech in Parliament.
2. No court proceedings can be instituted against a member for anything said or any vote given in the House or its committees.
3. This immunity applies to every statement made by a member outside Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 105 protects speech and votes in Parliament and its committees. It does not provide the same parliamentary immunity for statements made outside Parliament.
accepted.tq: Reject the overbroad extension of a privilege beyond its constitutional setting.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a collective privilege of a House of Parliament?
o: The power to exclude strangers and hold secret sittings
The right of an individual member to refuse to give evidence
Freedom from arrest in civil cases during and around a session
accepted.x: The power to exclude strangers and hold secret sittings belongs to the House collectively. The other listed privileges are individual privileges of members.
accepted.tq: Separate collective privileges from individual privileges before eliminating options.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A Member of Parliament enjoys freedom from arrest in civil cases during which period?
o: Forty days before and after a session and during the session
Only on the day of voting in the House
The entire term of the Parliament, without exception
Only during the recess between two sessions
accepted.x: The privilege covers civil arrest during the session and for forty days before and forty days after the session. It does not cover criminal or preventive detention.
accepted.tq: Test the exact time period and the civil-case limitation together.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The privilege of a House to punish members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt is a
o: Privilege available only to the Speaker
Judicial power of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The power to punish members and outsiders for breach of privilege or contempt is exercised by the House as a whole and is therefore collective.
accepted.tq: Identify whether the power belongs to the House or to an individual member.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an individual parliamentary privilege of a member?
o: Freedom from arrest in civil cases during the prescribed period
Freedom of speech in the House
Power to prohibit publication of the House's proceedings
accepted.x: The power to publish or prohibit publication of the House's reports and proceedings is a collective privilege of the House, not an individual privilege.
accepted.tq: Find the option that belongs to the opposite classification.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under Article 122 of the Constitution, courts cannot inquire into parliamentary proceedings on the ground of
o: The absence of a parliamentary session
accepted.x: Article 122 bars courts from questioning parliamentary proceedings on the ground of alleged procedural irregularity.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional Article with its precise limitation on judicial inquiry.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the present position regarding codification of parliamentary privileges in India?
o: All privileges have been exhaustively codified in a single statute.
Privileges are derived exclusively from judicial decisions.
Only individual privileges are codified under Article 122.
Parliamentary privileges are not codified, but continue under Article 105(3).
accepted.x: Parliamentary privileges have not been comprehensively codified. They continue under Article 105(3), with their historical basis in the privileges of the British House of Commons.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an uncodified constitutional position from a supposedly exhaustive statute.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sita Soren case of 2024:
1. A seven-judge Bench held that parliamentary privilege does not protect a legislator who takes a bribe to vote or speak.
2. The decision overruled the protection recognised in P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998) in this context.
3. The decision held that every speech made by a legislator outside the House is protected by Article 105.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The seven-judge Bench in Sita Soren (2024) held that privilege does not protect bribery for voting or speaking and overruled the contrary position in P.V. Narasimha Rao. Statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Use a recent judicial decision while rejecting an overbroad claim about immunity.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who has the power to prorogue a House of Parliament?
o: The Secretary-General of the concerned House
accepted.x: Prorogation, which ends a session, is ordered by the President. The Speaker or Chairman orders adjournment sine die.
accepted.tq: Separate the authorities for adjournment sine die and prorogation.
accepted.sec: Session terminology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A sitting of a House is suspended for a specified number of hours or days. This parliamentary action is called
accepted.x: Adjournment suspends a sitting for a specified period. It does not end the session or the life of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to a short procedural scenario.
accepted.sec: Session terminology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes prorogation from dissolution?
o: Prorogation ends a session, whereas dissolution ends the life of the Lok Sabha only.
Prorogation ends the life of both Houses, whereas dissolution ends only a session.
Dissolution is ordered by the Speaker, whereas prorogation is ordered by the Chairman.
Both prorogation and dissolution end the life of the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.x: Prorogation ends a session, while dissolution ends the life of the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is never dissolved.
accepted.tq: Compare the effect and authority of two easily confusable parliamentary actions.
accepted.sec: Session terminology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in the correct procedural sequence after the conclusion of the business of a sitting:
A. Prorogation by the President
B. Adjournment sine die by the Speaker or Chairman
C. Reassembly in a new session
D. Recess

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Normally, the Speaker or Chairman first adjourns the House sine die; the President then prorogues it, followed by a recess and later reassembly in a new session.
accepted.tq: Use the first-and-last method and distinguish a sitting, session and recess.
accepted.sec: Session terminology  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about parliamentary privileges is NOT correct?
o: A member may claim exemption from jury service.
The House may exclude strangers and hold secret sittings.
Members are protected from arrest in all criminal and preventive detention cases during a session.
Both collective and individual privileges exist.
accepted.x: Freedom from arrest applies to civil cases during the prescribed period; it does not extend to criminal or preventive detention cases. The other statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Look for the overbroad phrase that extends a limited privilege to all cases.
accepted.sec: Parliamentary privileges - Art. 105, collective and individual, Art. 122  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
